entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Wipe your boots outside the line, not across it. Thank you. People forget when they’re tired.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Because people lean over before remembering not to answer. Hollow Village draws drinking water elsewhere. The cover keeps children from the edge; the salt needs tending whether the lid is down or not.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Start at the Echo Well. The furnace carts used to wash their burial sacks there. We covered the mouth after the water began talking. Elin has opened a safe approach, but he won’t break anything with people still on the road. Neither will you, I hope.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: I say what I’m doing to the person beside me. “Pass the cloth. Hold the bowl.” Real things, with someone there to answer. I don’t work at the boundary alone anymore.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: More copied orders, and still nobody willing to stand here and explain them. I’ll keep the copies dry anyway. Elin is at the Old Cloister, beyond the Echo Well. He marked an approach with salt. Follow it, and don’t answer what comes out of the well.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Vesk sent word he’ll bring the broken ward parts himself. Good. There are people here who want to ask about them. Your way lies past the Echo Well to Elin at the Old Cloister. Keep inside his salt marks; the well has learned more voices than it ought to know.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Stay between the salt marks. Three dead carters came here with requisition freight from the Old Orchard. I buried them. Their tokens and my notes are beside the well; see if Mara can identify them.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Mila told me she’s using her own name at home again. That won’t stop the Caller borrowing the other one; they know to keep the door shut. You do the same at the Echo Well: don’t answer. Beyond it, Elin has marked the approach to the Old Cloister with salt.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: The cold furnace, nearest the loading bench. Handle a shard by its cloth. If it speaks, let it finish without helping it.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: At the Glass Quarry. There’s room around the cold furnace to compare rejects without anyone carrying molten work past your elbow. The Ash Steppe has plenty of open ground; we still manage to burn ourselves in the crowded bit.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: Behind the chalk mark. The floor looks cold because the heat is underneath it. Now, what broke?

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: That’s my stamp. We call it ward-glass. Bone ash, burial salt, a little bronze from a bell. The first cooled pane spoke in my apprentice’s dead father’s voice. Not all the voices are the Caller. Some are stuck inside, holding it back. Raut’s men watched a test at the quarry. The test bed and rejects are still there.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: So the apprentice can see where the crack started. Melt it at once and he’ll make the same mistake with twice the material. I mark my own failures too.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: The sacks are gone. The survivors took the lamp too. People here are angry about supper; I’ve told them whose flour we were eating.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: When a rope team can’t stand upright anymore. I send another if I have one. Anyone who promises never to stop has never had to send people out.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: The unsold sacks are under canvas. Nobody touches them until you’ve spoken to Hana.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: We pulled twelve out. Four are still missing. The helmsman says he saw two lights lining up a channel through the rocks. Hana keeps the true shore lamp. Ask her whether it moved before you let him put all of this on us. I’ve got enough people shouting already.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Ropes from the rocks. Boats would have rolled before we reached it. Wreckers’ Rest keeps shore gear for that. We don’t get to choose whether the sea leaves us men or cargo first.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: They agreed to the loan. Made me count every sack in front of them. Hana holds the tally and the lamp keys now. I’m not allowed to touch a signal alone.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: My crew put it there. They said an empty coaster was coming. I let them, and the coaster wasn’t empty. We’ve eaten some of the flour. I can turn over what remains with our names attached, or ask the survivors to leave it here as a debt while we repair the true warning light. They may refuse. I won’t hide the lamp either way.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: If you’re from the ship, there’s a dry corner left. If you’re here for cargo, take a number like everyone else.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Then no replacement keeper. I’ll prepare the cradle so it can be opened without trapping another voice. First Raut, then the glass. Warn the drivers before we start; some will choose not to make the journey.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Radek sent the dimensions of his three bells. They fit the unused connections. Castings are only half of it: Yara must have willing watches whose households can spare them. Otherwise I can take the binding myself, or we can break it without a replacement. The workers will need your convoy and the supplied posts.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: First capture and supply two posts, and destroy the raiding caravan. The commander may be defeated before or after this choice.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Raut is defeated. Decide what to do with the glass at the Old Cloister. That decision will end the campaign: finish any local business before making it.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Not on your order, or mine. A living keeper would have to understand the confinement and offer freely. I’ve spent long enough studying it to make that choice for myself. No one else owes it to me.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Radek has the bells; Yara has people willing to tend them. We still have to get them through. I’ll leave the binding alone until Raut falls and all three watches answer.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Keep your hand off that catch. It still works. There’s room beside me where you can look without touching.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Three bells can replace this binding, but only with Radek’s castings and Yara’s willing watches. Or I take it myself. I am offering, captain; you are not sentencing me. We can also break it all and send the dead away, with no ward left for the long road. Whichever we choose, your convoy must bring the workers and supplies. You can leave this undecided and come back.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: The families have kept their bell, but Yara has no shared watch to offer us. I won’t bind unwilling households to a rota. I can take the old binding myself, or we can free the dead without replacing it. We will need provisions at the cloister either way.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Yara has volunteers, and their families will eat while they stand watch. That makes the three-bell plan possible, if Radek has agreed to cast them. Without his bells there is still my offer, or breaking the binding outright. We need to agree on a method before asking the workers to set out.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Workers, salt, provisions, and a way to get them to the Old Cloister without losing them. Secure two posts, supply them with your convoy and destroy the enemy caravan. Then we can settle a plan. The binding work itself waits until Commander Raut is defeated.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: The supply posts are ours and Raut has lost his caravan. He still holds the fortress. You can agree on a plan at the Old Cloister now, but cannot carry it out while he controls the glass.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Radek’s single heavy bell will serve its own crossing. It cannot stand in for three separate watches. My offer still stands: I take the binding willingly. Or we free the dead without replacing the ward. Either method needs a work crew brought here safely.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: I know how far the old keeper could walk. I’ve measured it. Bring the stores when Raut is gone, and leave the door open to more than soldiers. Until then, the fastening stays loose.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: What I saw, then what kept me from seeing the rest. Fog, distance, a blocked lens. An empty gap is better than a confident guess someone will navigate by.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: One light gives a direction. Two aligned lights suggest a channel. That’s why spare red lenses stay locked away, and why I write down the bearing before I turn any screw.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Dren’s crew borrowed a portable lamp to search the shallows. Before the wreck, not after. I saw its red light above the wrong rocks that night and rang the warning, but the ship was already turning. Their lamp had a split carrying sleeve sewn with sail thread. If you find it, compare that seam.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Don’t lean on the bracket. It took an hour to set that bearing. You can lean on the wall; it’s less particular.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: It should be cold enough to handle now. Don’t let anyone call the second light a wandering soul. I know the color of my own lens.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: By touch. Cold fingers, poor breathing. People who can still argue about being moved usually aren’t first in need of it.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Wash your hands before touching anything. If you’re only here to talk, keep your voice below the coughing.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: I’ll take someone with me to the grave. If the print stops, it tells us he wanted his fare. It won’t tell us whether Oss did right.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: His daughter. I dried her by this stove. She said the ferry swung broadside and her father went over with the safety loop on his wrist. Oss had a knife in his hand. She couldn’t see what he cut. That is all she saw; don’t add to it. The token belongs in the shroud. I can see to that.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Raut’s quartermasters called it emergency ward-making. They took our burial salt first, then opened old graves. I counted what they took. When the bell cord wore through, there was nothing left to trade for a new one. The next consignment waits outside. We can stop it here, or mark the crates and let Orsa follow them to the buyer.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: There’s a cross burned beneath each handle. Orsa knows to look. I’ve kept enough salt for the door, but we’re cutting the last linen into strips.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: We dry them, mark where they were found and keep them apart. A recovered coat is not proof its owner drowned. Ask me before taking anything from the shelf.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: The crates are back inside. There’s salt at the threshold again, and the graves will stay shut. Orsa can check my quantities against what reached Saltmarket.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: I buried the keeper in spring. Oil still disappears from the supply shelf, and the light still turns in bad weather. No request for wages, no name on the tally. Before someone sends a patrol to stop a theft, would you see who’s up there? A stolen jar is cheaper than a dead traveler.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Star Monastery copied the maintenance instructions, but drawings don’t show every kind of wear. The used parts stay beside them. Ask to compare both before deciding a sketch is complete.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: There’s hot water, if that helps. Tea when the next delivery arrives. We’ve been saying that for a while.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Their petition hangs here with my name beneath theirs. The oil is counted openly now. They’re staying at the light while we wait for an answer.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: I can stand surety and ask for civilian service in place of punishment. I cannot grant a pardon, and neither can you. Their names will be posted where officers can read them. Or the Candlekeepers can keep bringing oil quietly, and the three stay hidden. The light gets tended either way; only one lets them ask to come down.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Look at the wick trimmings. A lamp left alone burns badly. If they’re fresh, someone is doing the job.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: A bed if they need one. Oil, if they’re working a lamp. My name if they’re accused. I try to find out which of those I’m promising before I sign.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: The oil goes up with the Candlekeepers. Three bowls come back scraped clean. I wish I could offer those people a place at this table as safely.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: If it were going to fall on someone. I’ve done it. Kept a sound piece for a stool, burned the rot. Being fond of a tree doesn’t mend its trunk.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: We’ve divided the rows, not the graves. She prunes too hard for my liking. I suppose she’ll say I keep every dead branch. We start together tomorrow.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: Not that branch. It only looks strong. Here, hold the twine if you want to talk.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The first pay is on my shelf. Feels odd. I can come to the tree whenever I want; the rest of the orchard is hers to manage. I’m trying not to watch.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: She could have dug first and argued later. I’ll give her that. Sharing means seeing her at my wife’s tree every morning. Wages mean asking permission to do work I’ve done for twenty years. I can live with either, I think. Which offer would you carry back?

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The older row breaks the wind for the younger one. I know which branches can go and which will bring a tree down. You can’t learn that by looking at the fruit for one summer.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: They’ve gone to sharpen their tools. That gives you a little time, not much. Don’t pull on a root if you find cloth.

entries.speaker: lida
entries.text: The woman who bought the orchard isn’t a fool. Half the trees no longer bear, and she paid with the price of her house. But my wife is under the oldest apple tree. When I said so, the cutters called it a trick. There are burial stones under the nettles. Find them before this becomes a fight.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: First capture and supply two posts, and destroy the raiding caravan. The commander may be defeated before or after this choice.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Because if I leave it in the strongbox, sooner or later I’ll call it repair money. Three purses are harder to spend by mistake.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Raut is defeated. Decide what to do with the glass at the Old Cloister. That decision will end the campaign: finish any local business before making it.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: You’re the captain? Good. Leave your boasts with the horse. I need someone who can get carts home.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Three carts. All the horses, every sack. Not one driver. Ren found black glass beneath the grain; I paid to carry barley, not that. Toman saw them pass Greenhollow. Find him. And if someone calls from the trees, look before you answer.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: Ren has put it in the empty stall. Nobody sleeps beside it. Bring me what you find, not a tavern story.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The Roadward Inn is our base in the Heartlands. Take two road posts, then bring the convoy close enough to supply each garrison. Break the enemy caravan as well. With the posts stocked and that raiding force gone, you can reach the fortress. Don’t mistake taking a post for feeding it.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: The supply posts are ours and Raut has lost his caravan. He still holds the fortress. You can agree on a plan at the Old Cloister now, but cannot carry it out while he controls the glass.

entries.speaker: mara
entries.text: So Ada buried all three. Leave her notes with me. I’ll tell the families myself. They have been setting places at supper; they need to stop waiting. The three purses are ready. You found what I asked for, captain. Give me a moment before we talk about the wagons.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: She called me Mila over breakfast. Then cried into the porridge. I stayed. The mittens fit, by the way.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: If that tear goes through the lining, give me a moment. I’m nearly done with this sleeve.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: We’ve spoken about the grave. She still uses the old name sometimes. I answer her when she’s beside me, not when something calls through the door. The neighbors can ask if they want to know.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: She measured my hand while I slept. I thought she was checking my fever. So she knows, and neither of us can bring ourselves to say it. I can ask her to call me Mila. Or let the old pet name stay between us, if we finally speak about whose grave the candle goes to. She may cry all night. I’ve been avoiding that more than the truth.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: The door stays barred. I tell her it’s cold. She tells me she knows. I don’t know which of us thinks that fools anyone.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Alya died on the road. I brought her scarf to her mother. The fever had left the old woman weak; she saw it on my shoulders and called me by Alya’s pet name. I stayed to nurse her. Never corrected her properly. Now Alya’s voice calls outside. Her mother left a bundle at the Echo Well. Please see whether it’s meant for a living girl or a dead one.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Some. People leave candles and things to take to the graves. I sew covers so they stay dry. Don’t move a bundle just to read what’s underneath; someone will think it’s been taken.

entries.speaker: mila
entries.text: Because cutting it down is easy. Asking whether they want it cut is harder. Sometimes they still want the old shoulders in it for a while.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
Yara left the bell with the displaced households and concealed their shelter from the patrol. They retain a close warning, but no common watch forms around the shrine.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Raut is dead. The convoy brings salt and provisions to the Old Cloister. Elin takes the binding of his own will, releasing the dead one by one from the glass. He can walk as far as the worn stone at the gate, no farther. Grain wagons pass beneath the renewed wards. Visitors bring him news, then requests, then disputes about whose cargo should go first. For now he refuses to sell passage. Mara sends the lost drivers’ wages home. She leaves a spare key with a Candlekeeper: the person who brings Elin bread must never become the only person allowed through his door.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila and the mother acknowledged Alya’s death but kept the household pet name. They know not to answer the voice outside. Their private comfort remains difficult to explain to neighbors.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: One returned bell yoke has an empty crown where its bronze was sawn away. Its village complaint lists disappearances after the removal. Raut marked the complaint “received” before renewing the same requisition. His personal share of paid escorts rises in the following weeks. A scorched courier tube holds a refused request to consult the old ward instructions at Star Monastery. This is not an inspector acting alone.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Six low stones follow the oldest row. Each names a burial; the planting dates are later. A storm-torn root holds shroud cloth, not a fresh body. The new survey pegs run straight across the graves. Felling and grubbing this row would disturb the burials, but the younger trees beyond it remain productive. Nothing here shows a curse.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A keeper’s copper wrist-piece is worn smooth on the inside. The servicing sketches show it fastened to a glass anchor at the Old Cloister, in Hollowvale. A living volunteer once bore the binding; later hands substituted the dead. Three independent bell watches can take over if all are maintained before the anchor is opened. Without either arrangement, breaking the anchor releases its captives and ends the glass protection. Repairs annotated over several generations agree with the wear on the fittings.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Water drips through a roof of woven reeds. Beside the altar, rescued clothing has been spread over benches to dry.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Iron-bound doors stand beneath the old storehouse. Wax flakes litter the steps, and damp has darkened the planks of the packing crates inside.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: This is the agreed plan, not its outcome. Defeat Raut to put it into effect. Local quests remain available until then.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Raut is dead. Behind the secured posts, Elin opens the binding and the convoy crews break the ward-glass. The last captive voices leave the Old Cloister. The Caller has no borrowed chorus there now; neither does the road have its old shelter. Drivers travel by daylight, pay more guards and turn back in bad weather. A winter delivery is lost to snow, another to men with crossbows. Two distant hamlets are abandoned before spring. Mara sends the lost drivers’ wages home and hangs a glass shard over the inn hearth, out of reach. Her next contract includes money for the drivers’ families.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The wicks are neatly trimmed. Three sets of wet boots dry beside narrow bunks; army patches have been cut from the coats above them. The watch tally changes hand every four hours. A rescuer’s rope is abraded where it ran over ice, and a child’s mitten is drying beside it. Three people are working here. Cut patches suggest desertion, but do not explain why they left.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Broken Glass

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila and the older woman spoke plainly about Alya’s death and began using Mila’s own name at home. They remain together. Naming the loss brought grief back into the room; it did not undo it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I chose Broken Glass. Once Raut is defeated and the work crews can pass, we will destroy the binding and free the dead. The road will lose its supernatural shelter; guards and good weather will matter again. For now, the glass remains whole.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The survivors allowed the food to remain as a witnessed debt, not lawful salvage. Dren’s crew must repair the warning equipment under Hana’s eye. The injured sailors still lack payment for what they lost.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
The bronze remains in storage. Radek cannot promise three village bells, and no one has agreed to collect or tend them.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: White stones mark the edge of an old burial mound. Ash has filled the shallow drainage channel, and dead grass clings to the damp bank.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
Radek cast one heavy bell for the busy crossing and returned the village deposits. Its single watch cannot replace the three separate watches required to free the road from one central binding.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I backed Toman’s warning in front of the carters. Greenhollow began checking its salt and bell rope; word of the chapel wrapping will also reach the soldiers.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Orsa withdrew the panels from hire and used her purchase fund for local wards. Houses will benefit first; long winter runs remain exposed.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The bell hangs from a low beam above five bedrolls. Its clapper is unwrapped; a fresh salt boundary encloses the sleepers. A woman shows the blister the hauling rope left on her palm. She agrees to return the bell to the shared frame if someone keeps watch there and meals are set aside for those who cannot take a turn. No one offers to leave the children alone again.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: An overturned hull shelters salvage crews. Wet boots steam by the stove, and salvaged lanterns crowd a shelf above the bunks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The three pay tokens match Mara’s numbers. Ada’s burial notes describe the same old scars Mara recorded. The drivers are dead; what killed them remains uncertain. Bone grit and shroud-thread cling beneath the washing ledge. Black splinters catch in the overflow, where a copper conduit leads toward the Old Cloister. Below the lid, a voice asks for the lead driver’s coat in the words Toman heard. That voice is not evidence of a survivor.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Two cart frames stand on the test bed: one glazed, one bare. Both salt lines were deliberately broken. Only the bare frame’s seat bears rope burns. The dated tally records two handlers lost from that frame after answering voices; the man inside the glazed frame remained at his post. Raut’s inspector countersigned the test and ordered another batch. Crushed coffin fittings remain in the mixing trough. Beran’s account, the chapel freight and the shipment weights fit together. The panels work as a fitted enclosure, not as loose cargo beneath grain sacks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
Lev publicly stood surety for the three keepers and petitioned for civilian service. Their names and Nika’s account are available to witnesses. No captain’s word has erased their charges.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The remaining cargo went to the surviving crew, with the false lamp and Dren’s account. The shore households must replace the food already eaten; the deaths are still for witnesses to judge.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Enough Bronze for Three
Radek cast the three small bells and set them aside for the villages. They can support separate watches using the Old Cloister fittings, but they still need willing keepers and a secured delivery route.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Thorn scrub fills the ground floor of a ruined watchtower. An old signal chain hangs through the stairwell, its lowest links polished by use.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Floodwater has left a brown line above the stone shelves. Swollen boxes rest in the mud, with brass fittings green from the damp.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The convoy leaves the fortress. Those who survived still need food, escorts and a way home.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Narrow arches overlook the snowfields. Candle grease coats the reading desks, and a worn bell rope passes through a hole in the ceiling.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Orsa reserved her existing glass for winter freight and canceled new purchases. I accepted continued use of the captive dead until we can reach the source of the binding.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
I carried Lida’s acceptance of shared cultivation. The graves remain untouched. Both women have a claim on the harvest and a reason to argue over the work.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I left Vesk in place to copy requisitions and concealed his help for now. The evidence survives in several hands, but villagers will have to wait to question the man who counted their losses.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Hairline cracks run through the old bell crowns beneath the soot. Striking them gives a dull double note. Once the iron yokes and ruined fittings are deducted, Radek’s chalk estimates fit: three small recast bells or one heavy bell with a spare clapper. The village deposits are separate from the unsigned garrison offer. The shortage is real, not a duplicate sale.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The crate holds salt-caked shrouds, coffin nails with wood still on them, and sacks of pale bone ash. A black panel fits its padded lid. The outward tag names Reed Chapel; the return tag names a furnace shipment through Saltmarket. These were not unused burial supplies. Someone collected them from graves, packed them carefully and sent glass back in the same crates.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Fallen apples soften in the cart ruts. A broken fence borders the oldest trees; several branches bear deep rope marks.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
Lev arranged quiet supplies through the Candlekeepers. The beacon remains tended, but its keepers still cannot visit the settlements without risking arrest.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss gave Ivet his account and stayed to train a replacement under her oversight. The family crosses without payment. Returning the token ended the wet prints; it did not settle responsibility for the cut rope.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
The workers stopped the washing line to repair the settling pit. Tessa will keep the lower well closed until repeated checks are clear. The lost wages are immediate; recovery is not.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Scarf That Came Back
Mila stays in the household under the dead girl’s pet name. The two women still have not spoken plainly about the grave.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
The cellar households moved into the loft before the clean spring channel was opened. The washing line continues, but the polluted well stays closed. Families have water and wages at the cost of their separate rooms.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Vesk agreed to face the village witnesses with the original returns. I promised an escort, not an acquittal. Raut’s trade is supported by freight, damaged wards, payments and testimony.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Black glass chips are ground into the sling beside barley husks. A broken panel is grooved to fit a wagon’s covered frame, not a window. The maker’s stamp matches a delivery docket from Cinderwell; the buyer is Raut’s convoy office. The burial crates traveled back empty of glass and heavy with chapel freight. The loading weights confirm both journeys.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ice grips the iron signal basket. Freshly split kindling lies beneath its cover, beside a watch stool wrapped in sheepskin.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Raut is dead. The supplied posts hold the route while the convoy carries Radek’s three bells to the waiting watches. Elin loosens the old binding only after each bell answers the next. The dead leave the glass; no living keeper takes their place. Yara’s volunteers mend ropes, dry salt and find replacements for exhausted neighbors. One village misses a watch during harvest, and carts wait two days rather than risk the silence. Mara sends the lost drivers’ wages to their families and hires another convoy. There is a road again, but keeping it open is work no victory can finish.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Black slag lies among broken furnace bricks. Wheel tracks run between the cooling pits, where discarded molds are stacked under torn canvas.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The yoke pins were withdrawn with a proper iron drift, not broken. Wool wrapped around the clapper kept it quiet. Two deep adult boot tracks lead toward the rear of the shrine; a drag mark stops at stone paving. A strip of flour-sack cloth hangs on the frame. Whoever took the bell meant to use it intact.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Under the unsold sacks lies the red lamp, wrapped in a split sleeve repaired with sail thread. Its foot is packed with the same white grit as the false bearing above the rocks. Fresh oil remains in the reservoir; the lens’s copper rim bears the observatory’s equipment mark. Beside it are tally sticks dividing the cargo before any salvage hearing. The lamp and repaired sleeve match Hana’s account. Who set the false light still needs to be established.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The bundle contains a candle tied with Alya’s hair ribbon and a pair of newly knitted mittens. The candle paper reads “For Alya’s grave”; the mittens are wrapped in a note: “Mila, these should fit this time.” There is no food for a returning traveler. The mother knows who died and who is living in her house. The voice outside has not changed that.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet marked the crates and copied their contents for me. We let one more shipment leave to identify its buyer; the chapel must stretch its scant burial stores until then.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The Cloister’s Prisoner

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A corroded brass gauge stands beside the tower steps. The lantern housing is scored by windblown sand; old tide marks stripe the lower stones.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Three sets of bootprints leave the wheel ruts. None returns. A torn salt pouch hangs from the lead cart’s broken rail; rain has washed a gap through the spilled line. Under a sackcloth scrap lies black glass wrapped in linen stitched for a burial shroud. A brass shipping tag bears the mark of Reed Chapel. There is no blood or sign of a struggle.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Weathered antlers crown the shrine gate. Bowls of porridge and patched blankets lie beneath a bare wooden bell frame.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Frayed cords descend into the dark shaft. Two clay bowls stand on the curb, and a loose stone rattles far below when the wind turns.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A brass fare token is sewn inside the coat lining. A length of ferry safety rope was preserved with it: one end snapped into fibers, the other was cut cleanly. The burial label says the body was recovered downstream with a loop still around its wrist. The token was not buried with him. The cut alone does not say why it was made.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: The glass anchor sits in a copper cradle, patched with the same black castings found in Raut’s freight. Burial cloth is fused into its layers. Elin briefly closes the old wrist-piece around his hand: the voices recede into a single strained breath. He opens it before the fastening catches. Three unused bell connections surround the cradle; their spacing matches the monastery sketches. All three alternatives require workers and supplies from outside. Opening the fastening before they arrive would leave the road unprotected.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Three Bells

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I helped Toman arrange shelter inside the tended boundary. The warning travels by trusted visitors tonight; travelers farther down the road may not hear it in time.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Second Shore Light
The salvaged cargo is sold a little at a time. The helmsman’s account of the second light remains untested.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss leaves the last crossing empty. The wet print keeps returning, and the passenger’s family has no account of his death.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
What Boiling Leaves Behind
Tessa carries water from farther uphill for the worst cases. The source of the contamination remains in use.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Fare on the Step
Oss agreed to an immediate hearing and suspended his crossings. Ivet returned the token and the prints stopped. Travelers must use the longer land route while another ferryman is sought.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Fir needles cover the roofless passage. A stone worktable survives beside the ruined chapel, its surface scarred by clamps and scorched wax.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
The Stag Shrine remains silent. Yara has no common watch to offer the road, and the scattered households fend for themselves.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I accepted Elin’s offer to take the binding willingly. He will replace the captive dead and remain confined to the Old Cloister. We must keep his supplies and visitors from becoming one person’s monopoly. The ritual requires Raut’s defeat and an escorted convoy; agreeing to it does not bind anyone.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Missing Warning
Yara and the families restored the shrine bell together. Hunters volunteered for a shared watch after meals were guaranteed for their dependents. These are willing allies for a future network, not people assigned to it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
Lida accepted wages while the buyer kept the deed. Toman witnessed unrestricted access to the graves. The burials are safe, but Lida no longer decides what happens to the living orchard.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
Three Pairs of Boots
The monastery keeps sending oil to an unanswered post. Whoever tends the beacon has no promise of another winter’s supplies.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: I committed the convoy to the Three Bells plan. Once Raut is defeated, Radek’s bells and Yara’s volunteers will take over before Elin releases the captive dead. The binding is still intact.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: A split settling pit leaks gray furnace wash directly into the lower well feeder. Upstream stones are clean; below the leak they carry a pale metallic crust. The older spring channel remains clear behind a silted sluice. Opening it would give clean water a separate route, but its overflow passes through the rooms workers have made in the old cellar. The leak, the deposits and Tessa’s cases point to ordinary poisoning.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Ivet withheld the next consignment and gave me her tally. The chapel keeps its remaining salt and linen; the buyer will know the supply has been challenged.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text: Old lime seals across the lamp bolts are unbroken. Its beam still meets the channel marker on the same bearing. A spare red lens is missing from the rack; its socket has fresh copper filings. The fixed light was not moved. A second portable lamp could have made a false alignment, but the empty rack does not identify who used it.

entries.speaker: narrator
entries.text:
The Roots Below the Deed
The sale remains disputed. Lida tends the trees she can reach; the oldest row goes unpruned while both households wait.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: You’ve still got feeling in your toes? Check before you answer. People like to be brave about the wrong things up here.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: It gives a bearing, not a path. Follow the markers through High Pass even when the light looks close. Frostspine folds the ground between you and it into places you can’t see until you’re in them.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: I guided that courier down and back. Raut broke the seal in front of us. Read the warning, asked how many wagons his glass could cover, and sent us away. On the return journey the courier heard her dead brother below the path. I held her coat until she stopped trying to climb down. Lev kept her copy at Star Monastery.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: I’ll sign for the boy and the rope. Not for battles I wasn’t at. That should still count for something.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Often. Cold makes people certain there’s a warm house just below the next ledge. A familiar voice can do worse. Get them somewhere sheltered first. Argue once they can feel their hands.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: Use my name. He already knows who carried the lamp. Tell Lev I want my good boots back when the courier can spare them.

entries.speaker: nika
entries.text: I’ve seen all three. Two hauled a boy out of a drift while the third kept the light. They left Raut’s unit after an order to strip salt from occupied houses. That part is their account; the rescue I saw myself. They’ll sign a petition if Lev stands surety. They won’t walk unguarded into the barracks.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Buying, selling, or asking why the price went up? I have different stools for each.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: The old panels stay listed in my books. Anyone hiring a covered wagon will know what covers it. Vesk at Crownbridge handled the requisitions; take him the test tally.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Seed, sometimes. Supper, I call a gift if I can afford it. Calling a gift a loan makes people hide from you at the worst possible time.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: I found Ivet’s burned crosses beneath the handles. The same carrier brought barley and took the marked crates back inland. His damaged freight and weighing sling are at the Tide Observatory. We can check him without tipping him off.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Saltmarket weighs the sale. The Tide Observatory weighs what a boat can actually lift without sinking. On the Salt Coast I prefer to compare the two before I pay for a missing half-ton.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Hana keeps the damaged pieces on the lower shelf. Don’t throw out the packing. It tells us which cargo traveled together.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: I can match the crates, but a mark doesn’t tell me what was inside. At the Tide Observatory they keep the weighing slings and unload damaged freight. Find the sling from the barley shipment. It carried twice the declared weight.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: Ivet’s next shipment never arrived. Good for her threshold; bad for quietly tracing the buyer. We still have the last barley load’s damaged freight at the Tide Observatory. Its weighing sling carried twice the declared weight. Start there.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: So the villages give up their burial wards and Raut sells passage to the people who can pay. I have two old panels and money set aside for more. I won’t order a new casting. But do I keep the old glass for winter freight, or put that money into salt and ordinary bell repairs? The second reaches more houses. It won’t shelter a cart between them.

entries.speaker: orsa
entries.text: The panels are locked away, and the repair orders have gone out. That won’t make the long stretches safe. Vesk at Crownbridge handled the requisitions. Let him see what they became.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: I’ve tied the boat up before sunset. First time in years I’ve been early for anything.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: Same handprint every dusk. No feet coming up to it. I scrub the step; it comes back. A man drowned here in the spring flood. The chapel has his things. See whether they kept his fare token. Maybe I’ve been leaving the wrong coin.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: My account is with the witnesses. The boat stays tied; I won’t take another fare while they hear it. No wet hand on the step now. Just people asking when they can cross.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: No print since the burial. Ivet checks the crossings, and the new hand is learning the knots. The girl takes the free passage. She sits at the far end.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: I cut it. The loop caught the rudder and held us across the current. There were four others in the boat. I could have tried another knot; I didn’t. His daughter knows where to find me. Ivet will hear my account with witnesses. I can go now and tie up the ferry, or stay under her oversight and teach another hand before I leave.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: Lantern Ferry has a crosscurrent you can see by day. After dark you only feel it when the boat turns. The shore bell warns of things on the bank; it doesn’t steer for you.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: Step on the plank, not the rope. If you need to be sick, use the downstream side. I’ve just cleaned this one.

entries.speaker: oss
entries.text: When the water reaches the second peg. Used to measure with my boot instead. The pegs don’t change their mind when someone offers more.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: IV. The Price of Passage

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Stay under Ivet’s oversight and teach a replacement. Give the family free passage, not excuses.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the sling and the damaged freight.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Cast the three village bells. I’ll carry your terms to anyone asking for them.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Go to the hearing now. Leave the ferry tied until another ferryman is found.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll examine the test bed. Keep the rejected pieces for comparison.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll follow the channel and look for where the two waters meet.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Ask her to use Mila. Take the candle together; you don’t have to leave her.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I. The Empty Seats

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll give Radek the actual weights and both terms.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look beneath the nettles. Ask the cutters to wait.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Show me where he left the cart. I’ll follow the tracks, not the voice.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What is left to do about the fortress?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Load what remains for the survivors. I’ll carry the lamp and your account with it.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look for his belongings at the chapel. Don’t make another night crossing alone.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Move the bedding first, then open the spring channel. No one sleeps below the overflow.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What do you keep in the Sealed Vault?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: III. Black Freight

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How much does it cost you to stand surety for someone?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I accept your offer. We’ll provision the cloister before you bind yourself.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why send freight to the Tide Observatory to be weighed?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Spend it on salt and bell repairs. Keep the panels as evidence, not merchandise.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why is the mill open after dark?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll ask Lev to stand surety and include what you actually witnessed.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep flawed castings instead of melting them again?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the shelter without bringing the patrol.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why not simply order every hunter to take a watch?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep the pet name if you both want it. But tell her whose candle you’re carrying.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: V. Who Keeps the Watch

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep old ward fittings alongside the books?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Mark this last load. I’ll follow it; don’t promise them another.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you cut down a tree you planted yourself?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Bring the families in first. Ask the Candlekeepers to pass the warning house to house.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Does a fine bell protect a village by itself?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Have you ever dragged someone back who begged to go on?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep tending trees that no longer bear?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Accept the paid care. Have Toman witness your right to reach the graves.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What has to be secured before the convoy can get through?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Three Pairs of Boots

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look through the salvage for the lamp and sleeve.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you choose who gets the bed nearest the stove?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: When can I take a road shortcut with the convoy?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can a ship mistake a house lamp for a channel light?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Take the evidence to them yourself. I’ll escort you, not speak in your place.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you ever refuse a fare?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep their names private. Ask the Candlekeepers to keep the oil coming.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What makes you refuse a cart that the driver says is sound?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll look at the bundle. Keep the door closed, even if the voice sounds kind.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you tell sickness from the Caller’s work?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Set aside food for their dependents. I’ll back the families’ place in the shared watch.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Scarf That Came Back

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Fare on the Step

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I need to go.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: II. What Was Taken from the Dead

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Return the token to him. I’ll ask Oss about the cut rope.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you go under for something that cannot be sold?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can you mend a cracked bell without recasting it?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: We break the glass and release them. No one takes their place.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What do you put in the log when you aren’t certain?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll inspect the shore lamp first. Keep the remaining cargo together.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll find Toman. Leave the glass wrapped until I return.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep this consignment. Give me your tally; I’ll take it to Orsa.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why mend a coat that will never fit its new owner?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Give me the key. I’ll compare the returned ward parts with the orders.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll examine the stored pieces before you choose a casting.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Are the cloth bundles by the well yours?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the frame. Keep the patrol away from the children until then.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What does Thornwatch watch besides hunters?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Cast the heavy crossing bell. Return the village deposits in full.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: When do you stop looking for a missing sailor?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How do you keep working when it calls in a voice you know?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you ever leave someone outside when the mill is full?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: How did your crew reach the wreck through the breakers?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can the Frozen Beacon be trusted in this weather?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Leave the bell with the families. Keep the patrol away from their shelter.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll read the copy. May I give Vesk your account with it?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Back the stoppage and repair the pit. Keep carrying spring water until the well is safe.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Roots Below the Deed

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep the missing drivers’ pay separate?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Tell her you’ll share the work and the fruit. Keep the burial row out of the bargain.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What do you need from a convoy captain here?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Stay and copy the orders. I’ll keep your name out of it for now.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Keep the old panels for the winter loads. No new glass, and no secret cargo.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why does the Echo Well stay covered?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Where do you test a new casting?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What happens to the things brought in from the river?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: We’ll bring the three bells to the village watches.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Would you put another person into that fastening?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Do you lend grain to people who might not repay it?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Missing Warning

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What Boiling Leaves Behind

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll check the broken crate. Keep its matching tags.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll take both offers to Lida. Keep the grave boundaries marked.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Ask for a food loan, openly. If they agree, have Hana witness the debt and the repair work.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Enough Bronze for Three

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll examine the well without answering it, then find Elin.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: What are you comparing in those jars?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Can anything still be recovered from the Drowned Archive?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: I’ll inspect the watch before anyone cuts off its oil.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Warn everyone now. Tell them exactly what you saw; I’ll stand beside you.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why tie up the ferry before the water gets dark?

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Stand surety. I’ll add Nika’s account and escort their petition, not promise a pardon.

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: The Second Shore Light

entries.speaker: player
entries.text: Why keep a damaged fitting after its cost has been entered?

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: I heard the families kept their bell. Fair enough, but that leaves Yara without a shared watch. I can still cast three village bells, if someone later finds willing keepers, or one heavy bell for the busy crossing. Metal won’t decide who gets up in the night.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Wait for the ring to die. There. Ask now. I can either listen to the bronze or listen to you.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three small bells will carry between nearby watches, if people keep the ropes and salt in order. I can cast them to the Old Cloister fittings. The heavy one will sound farther from a single crossing and need fewer hands, but the outlying houses won’t hear it. I won’t sell either as protection without someone there to ring it.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Vesk has the key and the weights. If he quotes the total without the iron, ask him to weigh it again.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Yara wrote about her rota and the meals for dependents. That is the first offer of keepers I can put a casting against. Three small bells would suit their shared watches and the Old Cloister fittings. One heavy bell serves a single crossing better. Choose the use before I pour; I can’t turn one into three afterward.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three villages paid deposits on funeral bells. Then the garrison offered to buy one big warning bell out of the same bronze. I haven’t promised the metal twice. I haven’t seen all of it yet. The returned pieces are in the Sealed Vault. Tap the crowns, not the skirts. It’s the part that holds the weight I need to know about.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: No. Someone checks the rope, clears the ice and takes the night turn. The bronze is my work. I make that part sound and tell them plainly what is theirs.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Three sound crowns. I’ve tested each one. They’re waiting for the watches and the wagons now. Tell Elin I kept to the old measurements; tell everyone else to bring dry rope.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: Sometimes a skirt. Not a split crown that has to carry the whole weight. At the Bell Foundry we keep the failed crowns on view. It discourages people from hanging bells with repairs they made in a hurry.

entries.speaker: radek
entries.text: The heavy bell rings true. The deposit money has gone back. It will do a useful job at one crossing. Not three jobs in three villages.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: A hot hub. A loose pin. A driver who only checked the side you can see. I don’t argue about it; I put his hand where mine was and let the wheel explain.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: First capture and supply two posts, and destroy the raiding caravan. The commander may be defeated before or after this choice.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: Raut is defeated. Decide what to do with the glass at the Old Cloister. That decision will end the campaign: finish any local business before making it.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: Hold the wheel. No, the wooden bit. Keep your fingers if you can; I haven’t got spare ones in the box.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: Discover the road stop first. Bring a sound convoy close, and clear nearby enemies and incoming shots at both ends before traveling. The shortcut takes you and the convoy together; it won’t pull a damaged cart out of a fight. To repair, stay beside the cart and hold the interact control.

entries.speaker: ren
entries.text: The supply posts are ours and Raut has lost his caravan. He still holds the fortress. You can agree on a plan at the Old Cloister now, but cannot carry it out while he controls the glass.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: I went under for a woman’s cooking pot once. Her son paid me in eggs for six weeks. He still brings one extra. Don’t tell anyone; I have a rate to maintain.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: Chapel tag. I hauled six matching crates out of the flood. They were stored in the Drowned Archive, where the upper shelves stay dry most years. One crate broke on the steps. Go look at what they packed beneath the shrouds. Mind the third step; it won’t bear you.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: Tags are on the nail. I keep them until I’m paid. Sometimes after.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: The upper landings, yes. The lower floor shifts when the current changes. In the Fens, the water brings its own furniture. If a stair was sound yesterday, that’s yesterday’s news.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: A Candlekeeper came through at dawn. Said Greenhollow had people sleeping under the mill stairs. I’ve sent dry sacks. As for your tag: six matching crates came out of the Drowned Archive. One broke on the steps. The packing is still there.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: If you dropped it in the river, tell me how heavy before you tell me how precious.

entries.speaker: sella
entries.text: Your warning got here before you. Now every wet footprint belongs to a ghost. The chapel tag is real, though: I recovered six of those crates at the Drowned Archive. One broke on the steps. Inspect the packing, not the stories.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: I ask what they ate, drank and heard, and who else is ill. I check what changes when I change one thing. The Caller exists. That doesn’t excuse me from checking the water.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: If you’re hurt, sit. If you’re here to explain a curse to me, hold that jar while you do it.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: The washing line is still quiet. We’re carrying clean water, and the cramps are easing in a few houses. Don’t let anyone drink from the well just because it looks better.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: Water from different households and different days. People tell me it all comes from one hill. The Ash Cairn marks where the channels divide. One hill can still give you very different cups.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: Take a stoppered jar for each side of the drain. Mark which is which before you come back. Not after.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: Cramps, vomiting, the same households every week. No voices. Their salt is dry. Boiling the well water hasn’t helped; the uphill spring water has. I need you to follow the old channel at the Ash Cairn. Don’t taste either sample. I already have enough patients who were curious.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: The channel is running clear. Six families in one loft, so there’s plenty of noise. At least they’re keeping their supper down. The old well stays covered.

entries.speaker: tessa
entries.text: That fits. Boiling won’t remove what the wash leaves in the pot. The workers will stop the washing line to rebuild the pit, but lose their pay meanwhile. Or we open the old channel now and move the cellar families into the dry loft. They’ve agreed, if their bedding goes first. Neither means the sick are cured today.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: That’s the mill’s coarse sacking. Two families took some to patch the shelter behind the shrine. One woman asked to borrow a drift yesterday. Said a hinge was stuck. They came from houses without a bell, and the shrine was left untended at night. Don’t send soldiers in after them. Speak to Yara once you’ve seen where they sleep.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: Wait there a moment. If I let this knot go, we start again. All right. Who sent you?

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: There’s an old man on crutches and three children. Knock on the stone before going round the back. They’re frightened enough.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: Since the warning, people won’t take the orchard path alone. That doesn’t make its roots cursed. I witnessed the sale; the buyer wasn’t shown the graves. Now she offers shared work and fruit, or wages for Lida to tend the burial row while the deed stands. Both offers are hers, not something I can impose.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: The lead driver stopped by the orchard. Said his wife was calling him in for supper. I knew her. Buried her last winter. He answered, climbed down, and the other two followed him between the trees. I rang our handbell. The horses came back. The men didn’t.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: Greenhollow takes people in when they miss the last safe stretch. The mill has dry floors and enough room to spread a blanket. The Old Orchard is beyond our tended boundary. In Greenmarch, distances on a map don’t tell you where you can sleep.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: Past the leaning apple tree. I stopped where our salt ran out. You won’t get me to pretend I went farther.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: There are people sleeping under the mill stairs now. We’ll manage. Sella at Mirecross knows the chapel freight. Go while the Candlekeepers make their rounds.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: So they walked away. Don’t tell their wives that means they’re dead. We call the voice the Caller. Salt without gaps and a bell with someone at the rope keep it off. Answer it, and you start wanting to follow. I can warn the road openly, or move the nearest households inside our boundary first. Moving quietly will take all night.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: I moved the pegs myself. This time both women saw where I put them.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: I witnessed the sale. The deed said “old orchard”; nobody showed her the graves. She won’t dig them up now she knows. She offered Lida two terms: work the younger rows together and divide the fruit, or keep the sale as it stands and pay Lida to tend the burial row. Lida hasn’t answered either.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: I put them where the flour ought to be. Then I ask the farmers for another dry shed. They swear at me. So far, they’ve always found one.

entries.speaker: toman
entries.text: The warning is up. Two drivers have refused to leave, which is better than losing two more. Sella at Mirecross handles the chapel’s river freight. Take her that tag.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Put it on the empty side of the desk, please. The other side is counted. I’d like one side of something to remain counted.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: The villagers own the deposits, not the castings. They agreed to take their money back if Radek chooses the heavy bell. If he casts three, each village must collect its own and maintain the hanging. I can release the bronze under either set of receipts. I can’t pay for ropes they forget to replace.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: A figure tells you the replacement cost. The part can tell you whether it wore out, was cut, or was never sound. Those are different questions, even when the total is the same.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Good. Ask him to put the soundness of the metal in writing. I don’t want another cracked crown on this shelf.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: The next copies will leave with ordinary freight. This buys us time, not forgiveness. Find Ada in Hollow Village; she can direct you to the Old Cloister.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: The dates agree. He read it, kept taking the burial stores, and collected his share. I can take these returns to the villages myself. They’ll have questions for me as well. Or I can stay at this desk and copy each new requisition before it leaves. If my name goes out first, I lose that access.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Returned stores, disputed deliveries, pieces too valuable to throw out. Crownbridge receives all three. Crownlands looks tidy on a map because the map leaves out the storerooms.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: I counted the sacks taken. Other people counted the missing. They sent me salt-crusted door ropes and broken bell parts with their complaints. I kept those returns in the Sealed Vault. Compare the dates with your furnace tally. The escort fees are there too.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Bottom lock sticks. Lift the key; don’t force it. I would rather not add a locksmith to the people I owe.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: The returns are packed with the accounts. I’ll go when the escort is ready. Ada in Hollow Village knows the approach to the Old Cloister. You still need to see the binding itself.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Orsa’s repair orders came through. She’s buying rope and salt instead of glass. It will help the houses, not the couriers between them. Raut’s knowledge is established by these dates and Nika’s account. I can take the evidence to the villages, or keep this desk and copy the orders still going out.

entries.speaker: vesk
entries.text: Orsa told me she still uses the old panels. Then our own freight relies on the same captive dead. I won’t leave that out of the account. Raut knew what he was doing; the dates and Nika’s testimony settle it. Shall I take the evidence to the villages, or stay here copying new orders under cover?

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: They still have the bell. The patrol has stopped asking me where they sleep. I can protect that much; I can’t offer Elin a shared watch we never made.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: Mind your ankle. There was a snare here this morning. I found the wire; still looking for the fool who laid it.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: Because one has a sick husband and another feeds five children alone. Put them on a list without asking, and you’ll have a splendid list and an empty watch.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: The bell is up. We’ve got a rota, and the dependents eat from the same pot as the hunters. Tell Elin we can teach other willing watches. Don’t tell him it runs itself.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: The shrine bell is gone. Not cracked. Gone. The patrol wants to search the children who gather antlers there. A child couldn’t lift the yoke, but that hasn’t slowed the patrol down. Go look at the frame. Tell me how it was taken.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: They used it better than we did. I have hunters willing to share a watch, but their dependents need to eat while they’re away. I can set aside part of the communal meat and open the shrine to the families. Or leave them the bell and keep their hiding place out of the patrol’s talk. Then there’s no shared warning here.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: They have snares to clear. I’ll keep them at it. Be quick.

entries.speaker: yara
entries.text: People who cut across the woods to save half a day. The Stag Shrine used to be their shelter. There ought to be a bell and a person on watch there. “Ought to” is the trouble.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Вытри сапоги перед полосой, не поперёк неё. Спасибо. Усталые часто забывают.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Веск передал, что сам привезёт обломки защиты. Хорошо. Здесь есть кому его расспросить. Тебе идти мимо Колодца эха к Элину в Старый скит. Держись его соляных отметок: колодец выучил слишком много голосов.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Говорю тому, кто рядом, что делаю. «Подай тряпку. Держи миску». Обычные вещи, на которые ответит живой человек. Одна у полосы больше не работаю.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Начни с Колодца эха. Печные обозы полоскали там мешки из-под погребальных остатков. Мы закрыли устье, когда вода заговорила. Элин расчистил безопасный подход, но ничего не ломает, пока на тракте люди. Надеюсь, и ты не станешь.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Опять копии приказов. А прийти и объяснить их некому. Всё равно уберу бумаги от сырости. Элин в Старом скиту, за Колодцем эха. Он отметил подход солью. Иди по нему. Тому, что заговорит из колодца, не отвечай.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Держись между соляными отметками. С грузом реквизиции из Старого сада привезли троих мёртвых возчиков. Я их похоронила. Жетоны и мои записи у колодца. Посмотри, сможет ли Мара их опознать.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Мила сказала, дома её снова зовут своим именем. Оклику это не помешает воспользоваться чужим; они знают, что дверь надо держать закрытой. И ты у Колодца эха не отвечай. За ним Элин отметил солью подход к Старому скиту.

entries.speaker: ada
entries.text: Потому что люди успевают наклониться прежде, чем вспомнят, что отвечать нельзя. В Глухой деревне питьевую воду берут в другом месте. Крышка не пускает детей к краю. За солью надо следить и с крышкой, и без неё.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: Моё клеймо. Мы зовём его обережным стеклом. Костяной пепел, погребальная соль, немного колокольной бронзы. Первая остывшая пластина заговорила голосом покойного отца моего подмастерья. Не каждый голос — Оклик. Некоторые заперты внутри и сдерживают его. Люди Раута смотрели испытание в карьере. Стенд и брак ещё там.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: За меловую черту. Пол только выглядит холодным, жар под ним. Так, что разбилось?

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: В Стеклянном карьере. У холодной печи можно сравнить брак, и никто не пронесёт расплав у тебя под локтем. В Пепельной степи земли сколько угодно, а обжигаемся всё равно в тесноте.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: У холодной печи, рядом с погрузочным столом. Бери осколок через тряпку. Заговорит — пусть говорит. Не подсказывай ему.

entries.speaker: beran
entries.text: Чтобы ученик увидел, откуда пошла трещина. Сразу переплавишь — он повторит ошибку на вдвое большей партии. Свой брак я тоже помечаю.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: На долг согласились. Заставили пересчитать при них каждый мешок. Опись и ключи от фонарей теперь у Ханы. К сигналам одному мне подходить нельзя.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Фонарь поставили мои. Сказали, идёт пустой каботажник. Я разрешил. А он был не пустой. Часть муки мы уже съели. Могу отдать остаток и назвать всех наших. Или попросить выживших оставить его нам в долг, пока чиним настоящий сигнальный огонь. Они могут отказать. Фонарь я больше прятать не буду.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Двенадцать вытащили. Четверых всё ещё нет. Рулевой говорит, видел два огня — будто створ через камни. Настоящий береговой огонь у Ханы. Узнай, не сдвигали ли его, прежде чем позволишь свалить всё на нас. Тут и без тебя криков хватает.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Если с судна — сухой угол ещё найдётся. Если за грузом — вставай в очередь, как все.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Непроданные мешки под парусиной. До разговора с Ханой никто их не тронет.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Мешки увезли. Фонарь выжившие тоже забрали. Наши злятся, что нечего на ужин поставить. Я сказал им, чью муку мы ели.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: По канатам со скал. Лодки перевернуло бы раньше. В Приюте корабельщиков на такой случай держат береговое снаряжение. Не нам выбирать, что море отдаст первым — людей или груз.

entries.speaker: dren
entries.text: Когда люди на канате уже на ногах не держатся. Если есть смена, посылаю смену. Кто обещает никогда не прекращать поиски, тот ни разу не посылал людей.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Значит, нового пленника не будет. Подготовлю люльку, чтобы её можно было открыть, не поймав ещё один голос. Сначала Раут, потом стекло. Перед началом предупреди возчиков: кто-то откажется ехать.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Не трогай защёлку. Она ещё работает. Рядом со мной есть место, оттуда можно посмотреть, ничего не задев.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Нужны люди для работы, соль, припасы и возможность довезти всё в Старый скит. Закрепи две заставы, снабди их обозом и уничтожь вражеский караван. Тогда договоримся о плане. Саму привязь тронем только после победы над командиром Раутом.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Три колокола заменят привязь, но нужны отливки Радека и добровольные дозоры Яры. Или я приму её сам. Это моё предложение, капитан, не твой приговор. Можно и всё разбить, отпустить мёртвых. Только весь тракт останется без защиты. Какой бы способ мы ни выбрали, людей и припасы должен привезти твой обоз. Не обязательно решать сейчас. Можешь вернуться позже.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Радек прислал размеры трёх колоколов. Подходят к свободным отводам. Но отливки — половина дела: у Яры должны быть добровольцы, чьи семьи могут отпустить их в дозор. Иначе привязь приму я. Или разомкнём её без замены. Для работы понадобятся твой обоз и припасы на заставах.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Семьи оставили себе колокол, но общего дозора у Яры для нас нет. Я не стану навязывать дежурство тем, кто не согласен. Могу принять старую привязь сам. Или освободим мёртвых без замены. Припасы в скиту понадобятся в любом случае.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: У Яры есть добровольцы, их семьи не будут голодать во время дозора. С ними план трёх колоколов возможен, если Радек согласился их отлить. Без колоколов остаётся моё предложение или полный разлом привязи. Нужно выбрать способ, прежде чем звать людей в дорогу.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Раут побеждён. Осталось решить в Старом скиту, что делать со стеклом. Этот выбор завершит кампанию: закончите местные дела до разговора с Элином.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Один тяжёлый колокол Радека послужит своему переезду. Три отдельных дозора он не заменит. Моё предложение в силе: я добровольно приму привязь. Или отпустим мёртвых без новой защиты. В любом случае сюда нужно безопасно доставить людей для работы.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Заставы снабжены, караван Раута разбит. Сам он ещё в крепости. План можно выбрать в Старом скиту уже сейчас, но исполнить его не выйдет, пока стекло у Раута.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Я знаю, докуда мог ходить прежний смотритель. Сам отмерил. Когда Раута не станет, привези припасы. И не оставляй дверь открытой только для солдат. До тех пор обруч не замкнут.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: У Радека есть колокола, у Яры — люди, готовые дежурить. Их ещё надо провести. Я не трону привязь, пока Раут не погибнет и все три дозора не ответят.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Не по твоему приказу и не по моему. Живой смотритель должен понимать, что останется здесь, и предложить себя сам. Я достаточно изучал привязь, чтобы решать за себя. Другой человек мне этого не должен.

entries.speaker: elin
entries.text: Сначала захватите и снабдите две заставы и уничтожьте вражеский караван. Командира можно победить до или после этого выбора.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: На кронштейн не опирайся. Я час выставляла направление. На стену можно, она не такая капризная.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Команда Дрена брала переносной фонарь — искать на мелководье. До крушения, не после. В ту ночь я видела красный огонь над другими камнями и ударила тревогу. Судно уже поворачивало. У их фонаря был лопнувший чехол, зашитый парусной нитью. Найдёшь — сравни шов.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Один огонь даёт направление. Два в створе указывают проход. Поэтому запасные красные линзы под замком, а перед поворотом винта я записываю направление.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Теперь уже остыл, можно брать. Только не слушай про блуждающую душу. Цвет собственной линзы я знаю.

entries.speaker: hana
entries.text: Что видела. Потом — что помешало увидеть остальное. Туман, расстояние, закрытая линза. Лучше оставить пропуск, чем уверенную догадку, по которой кто-нибудь поведёт судно.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Сушим, отмечаем, где нашли, храним отдельно. Выловленный кафтан ещё не значит, что хозяин утонул. Прежде чем брать с полки, спроси меня.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Прежде чем что-нибудь трогать, вымой руки. Если только поговорить — говори тише кашля.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: На могилу возьму кого-нибудь с собой. Если след исчезнет, значит, ему нужен был жетон. Прав ли был Осс — это по следу не узнаешь.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Ящики занесли обратно. На пороге снова есть соль, могилы больше не откроют. Орса сверит мою опись с тем, что дошло до Соляного торга.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Под каждой ручкой выжжен крест. Орса знает, где искать. На порог соли я оставила, а последнее полотно уже режем на полосы.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Его дочь. Я сушила её у этой печи. Говорит, паром развернуло боком, отец упал за борт с петлёй на запястье. У Осса в руке был нож. Что он резал, она не видела. Это всё, что она рассказала. Не добавляй от себя. Жетон нужно вернуть в саван. Я займусь.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: Интенданты Раута сказали: срочно делают защиту. Сперва забрали погребальную соль, потом вскрыли старые могилы. Я считала всё, что увозили. Когда перетёрлась колокольная верёвка, на новую уже нечего было выменять. Следующая партия ждёт снаружи. Можно оставить её здесь. Можно пометить ящики, а Орса проследит, кому они достанутся.

entries.speaker: ivet
entries.text: На ощупь. Холодные пальцы, слабое дыхание. Кто ещё может ругаться из-за переселения, обычно нуждается не первым.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: В Звёздном монастыре переписывали наставления по уходу, но не всякий износ попадёт на чертёж. Поэтому снятые детали храним рядом. Прежде чем верить полноте рисунка, сравни и то и другое.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Койки, если нужна койка. Масла, если он при лампе. Моего имени, если его обвиняют. Прежде чем подписывать, стараюсь понять, что именно обещаю.

entries.speaker: lev
entries.text: Есть горячая вода, если годится. Чай будет со следующей поставкой. Мы это уже давно говорим.

entries.speaker: lev
